#### Python

```{python}
#| label: bernoulli-variance-py
#| code-fold: false
#| fig-alt: "A dome-shaped curve of the variance of a Bernoulli random variable against its probability, for probabilities from 0 to 1. The curve is 0 at both ends and peaks at 0.25 when the probability is 0.5, which a dot marks."
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

prob = np.linspace(0, 1, 201)
variance = prob * (1 - prob)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 3.5), layout="constrained")
ax.plot(prob, variance, color="#1f77b4")
ax.plot(0.5, 0.5 * (1 - 0.5), "o", color="#ff7f0e")
ax.set_xlabel("probability of a 1")
ax.set_ylabel("variance")
plt.show()
```

#### R

```{r}
#| label: bernoulli-variance-r-alt
#| include: false
fig_alt <- paste(
  "A dome-shaped curve of the variance of a Bernoulli random variable",
  "against its probability, for probabilities from 0 to 1.",
  "The curve is 0 at both ends",
  "and peaks at 0.25 when the probability is 0.5,",
  "which a dot marks."
)
```

```{r}
#| label: bernoulli-variance-r
#| code-fold: false
#| fig-alt: !expr fig_alt
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 3.5
library(ggplot2)

prob <- seq(0, 1, length.out = 201)
bernoulli <- data.frame(prob = prob, variance = prob * (1 - prob))
mid <- data.frame(prob = 0.5, variance = 0.5 * (1 - 0.5))

ggplot(bernoulli, aes(x = prob, y = variance)) +
  geom_line(colour = "#1f77b4") +
  geom_point(data = mid, colour = "#ff7f0e", size = 2) +
  labs(x = "probability of a 1", y = "variance") +
  theme_minimal()
```

:::

The [variance](#def-variance) $\prob(1 - \prob)$ of a [Bernoulli](random-variables.qmd#def-bernoulli) [random variable](random-variables.qmd#def-random-variable),
against its [probability](probability-basics.qmd#def-probability) $\prob$.
It is 0 at $\prob = 0$ and $\prob = 1$, where the [outcome](expectation.qmd#def-outcome) is certain.
It is largest, $1/4$, at $\prob = 1/2$ (dot), where the outcome is least predictable.
:::
